title: run_in_terminal returns partial output for multi-line POSIX commands (RichExecuteStrategy resolves on first onCommandFinished)
body_clean:
## Summary

When the chat agent pastes a multi-line POSIX command via [INLINE_CODE] (for example a [INLINE_CODE] heredoc or a small [INLINE_CODE] script), the tool returns to the model after only the first line has run. The remaining lines continue executing in the terminal unattended while the agent moves on, causing empty/partial output, wasted follow-up turns, and incorrect patches.

## Root cause

[[INLINE_CODE]](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts) resolves on the **first** [INLINE_CODE] shell-integration marker:

[CODE_BLOCK]

Shell integration fires one marker per top-level statement. For a multi-line submission this means the strategy returns after line 1, even though the combined submission is logically a single tool call. Input detection in [INLINE_CODE] is unaffected (it reads the PTY directly), so interactive prompts still surface — but command completion semantics are wrong.

### When was this introduced?

The behavior has been present since the rich execute strategy was first wired up to shell integration in commit [INLINE_CODE] "Get rich strat working" (2025-07-14) and [INLINE_CODE] "Use command detection output and exit code". It was masked in practice by the nohup-compound corruption (#312202) for background commands; with that fixed, multi-line foreground heredocs now dominate the failure signal.

## Impact

Observed on eval run [INLINE_CODE] (terminalbench2, vscode agent). At least 8 of 25 failing instances trace directly to this bug, including:

- [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE], [INLINE_CODE]

Each of those produced an empty or near-empty patch ([INLINE_CODE]) after burning the model's token budget on spurious system-initiated follow-up turns triggered by early command completion.

title: Fix bugs in daemonset controller and e2e tests
body_clean:
This PR is a preparation to get daemonsets working on Mesos. On the way towards this, the following bugs were found and fixed by this PR:
- the e2e tests delete all node labels. Other e2e tests might rely on them, e.g. on kubernetes.io/hostname, or in the Mesos case on some other labels.
- the pods created by the daemonset controller don't have [INLINE_CODE] set, although the code suggests it should. Hence, they are scheduled by the scheduler first, hopefully onto the right nodes. During this time, the daemonset controller thinks again and again that the nodes have no daemon pod created yet. As a consequence, it creates more and more pods until it sees the already created daemon pods scheduled to the nodes which match the selector. In the case of a slow scheduler you easily end up with tens of pods for a 2 node setup.
- the daemonset e2e test checks for resource version conflicts and tries to update again. But it does not base the update on the newest version. Hence, when the version conflict occurs, the code won't be able to fix it.

title: Add support for Quotas on Running Pods
body_clean:
This is a continuation of a discussion started in the #sig-scheduling kubernetes slack channel between @davidopp, @smarterclayton, and @quinton-hoole.

Fundamentally the quota system prevents the 'creation' of pods but has nothing (as far as I can tell) to do with the 'running' of pods. There are lots of reasons why a pod can't get get to the 'Ready' state especially in a resource constrained cluster. What a 'running' quota would do is not penalize a given user/namespace for having pods that can't be scheduled.

A simple example would be a namespace with a quota of 4 pods that current has 2 ready/scheduled pods and 2 pods that can't be scheduled and may not be able to for quite a while. Given a the current quota system a new pod could not be created in this namespace. With a running quota system of 4, however, 2 additional pods could get scheduled.

I believe that this is the time to address this functionality because the addition of the JobController, and support for batch workloads in general, will increase the potential of a given Kubernetes cluster to be resource constrained.
